en: So in my project here, I have the problem
that I can't edit notes.
Of course, by the way, if you've been
following along in your own project, it very
likely looks differently, works differently,
and might be working. But here for me, it
isn't. Now, I already drafted a prompt I
could send to the AI, which will likely fix
those issues.
But before we do that, let's talk about
feedback loops.
When using coding agents like Codex, you
want to give your agents tools or
capabilities that allow them to
self-validate or verify their work.
Because it's not very good if you as a human
have to check everything. You should check
it all,
but you should ideally do that after the
agent did so. Because giving your AI agent
tools to
validate its own work allows it to run
longer and catch and fix many issues before
they reach you.
Now, there are different ways of allowing
your agent to self-verify its work.
You can allow it to
lint the project, to look for linting
errors. Or if you're using a type-safe
language like TypeScript in our case, you
can use type checks.
You can also allow it and tell it to build
the project from time to time, build it for
production, compile it so that it can catch
errors from that.
And we're doing all these things in our
project. Our agent does that all the time.
But there's more.
Automated tests can come to mind because of
course, if your project contains unit and/or
end-to-end tests,
the AI agents can run those too and can
catch errors from those tests and then fix
the underlying reasons.
And you could also give your agent access to
the browser. You could allow it to use the
browser, for example, with tools like the
Playwright MCP, which is something I'll get
to in a later lecture though. For now, let's
focus on the automated tests.
